decisions.reason: The connector-placement rules are already limited to the three-board variant, which remains retained alongside the new integrated-board variant.
The source adds an integrated-board variant without removing or changing the existing sensor-board fit requirement.
The source proposes a separate integrated PCB variant but does not change the existing enclosure required to accommodate the three-board device.
The existing power-board mechanical constraints remain applicable to the retained three-board variant and are not altered by adding a separate integrated-board variant.
Retaining the same functionality does not specifically establish antenna placement for the integrated-board variant, while the existing main-board antenna requirement remains unchanged.
The source does not specifically decide whether the integrated cost-reduced board must retain the development breakout, and it does not alter the existing main-board breakout requirement.
The main-board dimensions and routing constraints remain historical requirements for the retained three-board variant; no integrated-board dimensions are established.
The source does not establish a layer count or grounding strategy for the integrated board and does not change the existing power-board stack.

The interboard power interface is explicitly scoped to the three-board variant, which remains retained; the new variant's lack of interboard connectors is already represented by the architecture Requirement.
The interboard signal interface remains valid for the retained three-board variant, while the integrated variant's elimination of interboard connectors does not modify that scoped interface.
The source proposes the integrated PCB design but does not request or change its production-export deliverables.
The client directly adds a component-selection preference for the integrated board to use JLCPCB Basic components as much as possible.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I was thinking that, if you have availability for another project and are interested, we could create the cheapest possible single board for this project. Everything would be placed on one board, and from the beginning we would try to use JLCPCB Basica components (as much as possible). There would be far fewer connectors because interboard connectors would no longer be needed. If you have ideas for making anything better or less expensive while retaining the same functionality, you can suggest them. I can create a new milestone within this project, and we can agree on the price. What do you think—does this approach make sense?

value_updates.integrated_board_jlcpcb_basic_component_: use JLCPCB Basic components as much as possible
